html:
Levuka, on the island of Ovalau, was the first European settlement and port in Fiji and its colonial capital from 1874 to 1882. Whalers and traders settled there from the 1820s and 1830s.

It was a rough port town of traders, planters and missionaries, and the place where Cakobau's kingdom met its debts. The Deed of Cession was signed nearby in 1874.

The steep hills left no room to grow, and the capital moved to Suva in 1882. Levuka stayed small, which kept its old wooden shopfronts. In 2013 it became Fiji's first UNESCO World Heritage Site. See also copra.
